 COMMON JUDGMENT

The above appeal has been filed by the insurance company challenging the award passed by the Tribunal and the Cross Objection has been filed by the claimants challenging the quantum of compensation passed by the Tribunal in M.C.O.P. No. 262 of 2017 dated 17.08.2021.
2.The

claim petition has been filed stating that on 08.11.2016, when the deceased and his daughter were travelling in a two wheeler bearing Registration No.TN 30 S 5776 in Mettur to Mechery Main road, a lorry bearing Registration No. TN 45 AE 2676 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, hit the two wheeler from behind as a result of which the deceased died on the spot and the his daughter suffered severe injuries all over her body and thus, the claim petition has been filed seeking compensation.
3. The sixth respondent in the appeal was set exparte before the Tribunal.

The New India Assurance Co.Ltd vs Ambika on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88855228/
2 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA No. 480 / 2022 & Cross Obj No. 76 /
4.The appellant / first respondent filed a counter in the claim petition denying all the averments made in the claim petition and stated that in any case, the claim was excessive.
5.The claimants examined three witness on their side and marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.

sentences.text:
The insurance company examined two witnesses on its side and marked Ex.D.1 to Ex.D.3.
6.The
Tribunal after considering the oral and documentary evidence filed on both sides found that the claimants are entitled for a compensation of Rs.1,06,17,075/- to be paid by the appellant.
Aggrieved by the said order, the appellant had preferred the instant appeal and the claimants had preferred the cross objection.

7.The learned counsel for the appellant / insurance company submitted that the Tribunal had taken the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.82,970/- based on Ex.P.9, the pay certificate issued by the TANGEDCO.

As per the said certificate, it is very clear that the last drawn pay of the deceased as on 08.11.2016 was Rs.70,153/- However, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA No. 480 / 2022 &
Cross Obj No. 76 / the Tribunal had erroneously taken Rs.82,970/- as income which was the notional pay fixed by the department only for sanctioning terminal benefits, and that the Tribunal ought to have taken the actual salary drawn by the deceased which was Rs.70,153/-.
The learned counsel submitted that in all other aspects the award of the Tribunal is just and need not be interferred with.

8.The learned counsel for the respondents 1 to 5 / cross objectors per contra submitted that the Tribunal had rightly fixed the monthly income at Rs.82,970/- since the deceased was entitled to a pay revision.
The learned counsel further submitted that filial consortium for the parents and parental consortium for the children ought to have been awarded at Rs.40,000/- each.

9.This Court finds on perusal of the oral and documentary evidence on record finds that the short question involved in this appeal is whether the Tribunal was right in fixing the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.82,970/-.
The deceased was working as a Assistant Executive Engineer in Tamil Nadu Generation and Distribution Corporation Ltd. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

sentences.text: CMA No. 480 / 2022 & Cross Obj No. 76 /
The cross objectors / claimants have produced Ex.P.9 pay certificate issued by the Senior Administrative Officer, TANGEDCO.
The pay certificate shows that the actual pay that was drawn by the deceased as on 08.11.2016 when the accident took place, was Rs.70,153/-.
The pay certificate also shows that as per the pay revision, the notional income of Rs.82,970/- was taken only for the purpose of sanctioning terminal benefits.

The relevant note reads as follows;
New pay notionally fixed with effect from 01.12.2015 but monetary benefit with effect from 01.10.2017 onwards.
By Diamond Jubilee Incentive Increment, pay to be fixed as Rs.82,900/- on the date of death for sanctioning TERMINAL BENEFITS only.
From the above note, it is clear that the amount of Rs.82,970/- was notionally fixed for the purpose of sanctioning terminal benefits and this cannot be considered as income of the deceased.

Therefore, this Court is of the view that the Tribunal ought of have taken the actual pay drawn by the deceased which is Rs.70,153/- per month The New India Assurance Co.Ltd vs Ambika on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88855228/

10.As regards the compensation under the head 'Loss of Consortium', the Tribunal awarded Rs.44,000/- towards loss of consortium for the first respondent in the appeal.
However, the Tribunal ought to have awarded Rs.40,000/- each for all the claimants under the head loss of consortium.
Thus, the award under the head loss of consortium is enhanced to Rs.2,00,000/-.
The award under the other heads are just and remains unaltered.

Thus, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as follows:

With the above modification, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the cross objection is partly allowed and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.1,06,17,075/- is hereby reduced to Rs.94,08,374/- together with interest at 7.5% per annum (excluding the default period, if any) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The appellant is directed to deposit the award amount now determined by this Court along with interest and costs, less the amount already deposited, if any, within a period of six (6) weeks from the date of a receipt of copy of this Judgment, if not already deposited and permitted to withdraw the excess amount if any deposited earlier.

On such deposit the respondents 1 to 5 are permitted to withdraw the award amount along with proportionate interest and costs, less the amount if any, already withdrawn as per the apportionment fixed by the Tribunal.

The share of the respondents 2 and 3 shall be deposited in the interest bearing Fixed Deposit in any Nationalised Bank till they attain the age of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis CMA No. 480 / 2022 & Cross Obj No. 76 / majority and the first respondent is permitted to withdraw the interest once in every six months.
No costs.

Consequently,
the connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
